bluf: Semahead is a Warsaw SEO and PPC agency whose domain, semahead.agency, now resolves to wenet.pl, the site of WeNet, a Warsaw web and marketing provider for Polish SMEs; the record dates no merger, acquisition or domain transfer. The successor sells websites, local marketing, SEO, Google Ads and AI visibility to small firms; its latest moves are a planned merger with WebWave sp. z o.o. (2026-08) and the Moje Opinie review product (2026-09). All 17 clients on record are names only. For a rival: the Monsoon read puts it at Landfall (75) with displacement 86, so the book very likely buys on price.
doing:
The positioning line reads 'Now WeNet: a technology partner for Polish SMEs, building websites, Google and AI visibility and business tools through one partner': in plain words, one vendor for a small firm's website, Google presence, AI presence and business tools. The headline claim, 'Over 70,000 entrepreneurs served and more than 50,000 websites designed', is a volume claim quoted as the site makes it; the record lists no founding year, employee count or owner.

The sold mix leads with Web & Product and Local, both scored 3: websites head the service list and the homepage claims 50,000+ sites designed; the local line has a case category with Google listing cases for Moonlight, Ajot and Auto Serwis Wesoła. SEO, Paid Search and AI Search / GEO score 2 each, with Wanpol at +355% TOP-50 phrases and Soprema into Google TOP 10, Al Fuego at 16,400+ clicks and 3,000 conversions, and the lead case Larkis reporting 113 phrases in AI. Four proprietary products are named: Netskaner (a free visibility check), Moje Opinie (automatic Google review collection, with Polskie ePłatności), the WeNet AI assistant that collects quote requests, and WeNet Club (SMB benefits). The record lists no partners.

Its AI posture is retail: it sells AI visibility to SMBs alongside SEO, publishes GEO and AEO explainers, and launched the quote gathering assistant in May 2026; the Horus read marks P1 partial because no audited AI visibility product shows.

Dated moves, oldest first, all dated by the sitemap: Michał Wrzesiński returned as president of WeNet Group SA (2025-02); Joanna Płona, named as WeNet Group president, presented a new strategy and the group took a majority stake in Firmao (2025-07), the succession unexplained; the 'Otwórz firmę na internet' image campaign launched (2025-10); the AI assistant launched (2026-05); a notice of the planned merger with WebWave sp. z o.o. appeared (2026-08); Moje Opinie and a partnership with DIMAQ's e-marketing academy followed (2026-09).

Pricing signals are promotional, not a model: a free Netskaner check, a free consultation and a July 2025 Nest Bank tie up offering SMBs up to 900 zł back on online presence spend; P5 reads unknown. Conspicuously absent: captured news entries, job listings or an ATS (none listed), partners, any data, CRO or content and PR capability (all scored 0), and any mention of Semahead on the captured WeNet pages, which leaves thirteen legacy case entries dated 2021-10-04 to 2024-10-24 under one generic title as the brand's only trace.

The verticals listed are manufacturing and building materials, restaurants and food producers, dental, automotive services, fashion and footwear ecommerce, and garden wholesale.

The needs read names 17 clients, all from case study pages on wenet.pl, and reads every one as engagement named only: 17 of its 17 clients are names only, with 0 observed, because the case rows carry no title or excerpt describing the work. No client on the record sits on another tracked agency's book (shared 0). What the base needs next, hedged: under KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation), it is likely that these local and web clients next ask for presence in AI answers, the line the Larkis case already sells; under KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer), it is likely, with moderate confidence, that the Google Ads hours sold to Al Fuego and its kind are absorbed by platform automation, leaving reviews, listings and first party data as the work. The absence of described work is a question to ask its clients, not evidence of thin work.

openings:
The strongest opening is the transition: brand status is merged, semahead.agency resolves to wenet.pl, and captured WeNet pages never mention Semahead, so a client that bought Semahead SEO or PPC work is very likely, with moderate confidence, being serviced under a different brand and proposition, and clients in a transition answer the phone. The falsifier: a captured WeNet page that names Semahead, dates the transfer and shows the same team on the account.

The book buys on price: displacement 86.4 on the Monsoon read, an observed Landfall band, so an offshore delivered rival can almost certainly undercut the website and local lines hour for hour, and no onshore claim on the record blunts the pitch. The verticals it names, dental, automotive services, restaurants and food producers, manufacturing and building materials, are contestable because all 17 clients are names only and no described work anchors them.

Gaps to lead with: it sells AI visibility with no audited product (P1 partial), so a rival with a citation share number leads with the number; no feed, schema or entity work shows (P2 absent); and no public pricing model (P5 unknown) means an outcome priced offer is a conversation it cannot have in public. Its paid search line is the most exposed under KJ4 and the record shows no test of ads inside assistants (P8 absent); a rival showing holdout results there likely sets the price, low confidence given SMB budgets.
